items.stem: Suppose ε₁, ε₂, …, εₙ are i.i.d. N(0, σ²). Consider Y₁, …, Yₙ defined by Y₁ = μ + ε₁ and Y_{j+1} − μ = ρ(Y_j − μ) + √(1 − ρ²) ε_{j+1}, j = 1, 2, …, n − 1. Let T = (1/n)ΣYᵢ. Suppose 0 < ρ < 1 and σ² > 0. Then for n ≥ 2
statements: T has mean μ and variance σ²/n
T ~ N(μ, δ²) where δ² > σ²/n
items.explanation: This is a stationary Gaussian AR(1) series. Its sample mean is normal with mean μ, and positive autocorrelation inflates its variance above σ²/n, so A, C and D hold and B ignores the correlation.

A.why: Each Yᵢ is a linear combination of the normal εs, so T is normal.

B.why: The Yᵢ are positively correlated (Cov(Yᵢ, Yⱼ) = σ²ρ^{|i−j|}), so the variance exceeds σ²/n.

C.why: Each Yᵢ has mean μ and variance σ² (the recursion preserves it), and Var(T) = σ²/n + (2σ²/n²) Σ_{i<j} ρ^{j−i} > σ²/n.

D.why: T is normal (statement A) with mean μ and a variance δ² above σ²/n (statement C).
